title: IMA seeks review of Sunny Deol starrer Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak; raises concerns over portrayal of doctors and hospital violence
raw_summary:
The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has raised objections to the promotional content of Sunny Deol’s upcoming crime drama Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, expressing concern over its portrayal of the medical profession. In a formal communication, the association questioned whether the film’s depiction of alleged corruption and violence against healthcare workers could contribute to negative perceptions of doctors and hospital personnel.

The IMA has outlined four key areas of concern, including the generalisation of alleged misconduct across the medical fraternity, the depiction of physical assaults on healthcare workers, the safety of medical personnel and the potential impact on doctor-patient trust.

In its letter, the association cautioned against portraying individual instances of wrongdoing in a manner that could reflect on the wider medical community. It stated, "The portrayal risks creating the impression that corruption, unethical practices, and alleged corruption in medical fraternity. While individual misconduct must be investigated and punished, the actions of a few must not be used to tarnish the reputation of countless honest and dedicated doctors."

The organisation also expressed concern over scenes involving physical confrontations in medical facilities, particularly if such actions are presented as justified. The IMA stated, "Scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff, and hospital personnel, particularly when presented as heroic or justified acts, risk normalising violence against those committed to saving lives."

Highlighting the safety concerns faced by healthcare workers, the association further said, "Doctors and healthcare personnel already face serious safety challenges in hospitals. Content that appears to glorify attacks on medical professionals may encourage hostility and further endanger those providing essential healthcare services."

The IMA also flagged the possible impact of such portrayals on public confidence in medical professionals, stating, "Such portrayals may foster unwarranted mistrust and hostility towards doctors, weakening the mutual trust and cooperation essential for effective treatment and healthcare delivery."

While making its objections known, the association clarified that it does not support unethical medical practices and that individual cases of misconduct should be addressed through statutory and disciplinary mechanisms. It argued that such instances should not lead to broad portrayals that could affect the reputation of the profession or discourage aspiring medical students.

As part of its appeal, the IMA requested an impartial review of the film’s content and asked for appropriate corrective measures to address its concerns. It also called on the relevant authorities to consider further action, stating, "In view of these concerns, we respectfully request... [an] impartial review of the film's content and its portrayal of the medical profession; seek appropriate corrective measures from the filmmakers to address the generalisation of alleged misconduct and the depiction of violence against healthcare workers; [and] consider a ban or other appropriate action if justified under applicable law."

Directed by M. Padmakumar in his Hindi directorial debut, Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak is an official remake of the 2018 Malayalam crime thriller Joseph. The film stars Sunny Deol as a retired police officer who investigates disturbing revelations involving medical malpractice and systemic corruption following a personal tragedy. The supporting cast includes Ravi Kishan, Pragya Jaiswal, Manish Wadhwa and Jisshu Sengupta.

Produced by Kamal Mukut, the film is scheduled to release theatrically on November 20, 2026. The IMA’s objections have brought attention to the film’s portrayal of healthcare workers ahead of its planned release.

title: Saif Ali Khan sells Bandra west apartment for Rs 4.11 crores
raw_summary:
Actor Saif Ali Khan has sold a 797 sq ft carpet-area apartment in Mumbai’s Bandra West for Rs 4.11 crores. The transaction also includes two open parking spaces, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.

The sale deed was executed and registered on October 19, 2026. However, the agreement to sell was signed on March 7, 2024, and registered on March 11, 2024. The buyers took possession of the apartment on March 7, 2024. The transaction attracted stamp duty of Rs 24.66 lakhs, as per the registration records. The apartment is located in Hi-Cons Residency, a residential building in Bandra West.

According to property registration records, Khan had purchased a 6,000 sq ft carpet-area unit spread across two higher floors of the same building from developer Hi-Con Constructions on March 30, 2007. The property was acquired for Rs 9.7 crores and included parking facilities.

The original unit was subsequently divided into three separate apartments on June 19, 2014. These comprised a flat measuring approximately 2,997 sq ft on a lower floor, another apartment measuring 2,205 sq ft on the same floor, and the 797 sq ft apartment that has now been sold. According to CRE Matrix, the original purchase price of Rs 9.7 crores covered all three apartments.

Saif Ali Khan’s Other Real Estate Transactions

Apart from the Bandra West sale, Khan has also leased commercial property in Mumbai. According to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix, the actor leased two commercial units spanning 5,692 sq ft of RERA carpet area on Andheri Kurla Road to Durva Fintech Private Limited for a monthly rent of Rs 22.76 lakhs.

The leave and licence agreement was registered on September 29, 2026, for a five-year period, from May 10, 2026, to May 9, 2031. The documents identify Vikaas Mohan Sachdeva, a director of Durva Fintech, as the licensee. Khan acted as the licensor through his constituted attorney.

Khan also owns an apartment in Mumbai’s Satguru Sharan building, where he lives with his family. The over 6,500 sq ft residence was purchased from real estate developer Satguru Builders in April 2012 for Rs 23.50 crores, according to property index-2 documents accessed by IndexTap.com.

Before moving to Satguru Sharan, Khan and his wife, Kareena Kapoor Khan, lived in the Fortune Heights apartment complex in Bandra. In April 2016, the actor purchased an apartment measuring more than 950 sq ft in the complex for Rs 7 crores, according to property registration documents accessed by Zapkey.com.

title: Diljit Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour hits roadblock as Delhi Police deny permission for October 30 concert
raw_summary:
Diljit Dosanjh’s upcoming Delhi concert has hit a roadblock after the Delhi Police denied permission for his October 30 show at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. The concert is part of the singer’s Aura India Tour and was scheduled to mark the beginning of its India leg.

According to reports, the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District) communicated the decision to ticketing partner BookMyShow. The police cited security concerns, including specific threat-related inputs and existing law-and-order commitments during the ongoing festive season.

The communication also referred to other law-and-order concerns while declining the request to hold the concert at the stadium. Why was Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert denied permission? The police decision comes after reviewing an application submitted by the organisers on October 14. The DCP's office cited multiple factors behind the refusal, including specific threat-related inputs, security and law-and-order commitments during the festive season, and other important law-and-order concerns.

The nature of the specific threat inputs has not been publicly detailed. Reports have also previously referred to security concerns surrounding Diljit, including alleged threats linked to Khalistani elements. However, the police communication does not publicly establish that any particular threat was directed at the singer or the concert.

The development comes amid wider security concerns in Delhi and recent incidents involving the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, including reports of shots being fired outside the residence of Diljit’s manager and an attack involving actor Tiger Shroff. Diljit’s Delhi show was earlier moved from November 1 The Delhi concert was originally scheduled for November 1 but was later brought forward to October 30. The date change followed an appeal by Rajya Sabha MP Vikramjit Singh Sahney, who had raised concerns about holding the concert on November 1, the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence. The organisers subsequently announced the October 30 date, with existing tickets remaining valid for the rescheduled show. Will Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert be cancelled? As of October 22, the denial of police permission does not by itself confirm that the concert has been cancelled. There has been no confirmed announcement from the organisers regarding a new date, an alternative venue or a complete cancellation of the Delhi show. Reports noted that the event listing continued to appear on BookMyShow, although the listing does not amount to confirmation of police clearance.

Fans who have already purchased tickets will have to wait for an official update from the organisers and BookMyShow regarding the status of the event and any possible changes to their bookings.

The locality is known for its coastal setting, residential developments and proximity to Mumbai’s entertainment industry. Versova has also emerged as a preferred location for professionals and families due to its infrastructure and access to key parts of the city.

Details Of Sonu Sood’s Rental Agreement

As per the registration documents, the rental agreement includes a year-on-year increase in rent over its five-year term. The monthly rent has been fixed at Rs 5 lakh for the first year. It will increase to Rs 5.40 lakhs in the second year, Rs 5.83 lakh in the third year, Rs 6.29 lakhs in the fourth year and Rs 6.80 lakhs in the fifth year.

The rental structure reflects an annual escalation of approximately 8 per cent. The agreement also includes a security deposit of Rs 32 lakhs. The transaction involved a stamp duty payment of Rs 93,000 and registration charges of Rs 1,000.

Versova is connected to several parts of Mumbai through Link Road, SV Road and the Western Express Highway. The Versova Metro station and Andheri railway station provide access to different residential and commercial areas across the city.

Its social infrastructure includes Versova Beach, cafes, restaurants, retail outlets, educational institutions and healthcare facilities. The proposed Versova-Bandra Sea Link is expected to improve connectivity across Mumbai’s western suburbs once completed.

The area’s combination of urban amenities, coastal surroundings and proximity to entertainment hubs has contributed to its appeal among residents and professionals.

Apart from his real estate transaction, Sonu Sood has maintained a presence in the entertainment industry as an actor and film producer. He has worked across Hindi, Telugu, Tamil and Kannada cinema.

title: Aastha Tiku’s directorial debut Dreamboat to premiere at Dharamshala International Film Festival; first look out
raw_summary:
Aastha Tiku’s directorial debut Dreamboat is set to have its world premiere at the Dharamshala International Film Festival (DIFF), which will take place from October 29 to November 1, 2026. The 24-minute fantasy comedy-drama stars Sofia Ashraf, Supriya Joshi, Tenzin Dalha and Prayrak Mehta.

Written and directed by Tiku, Dreamboat follows an underground musician whose unconventional relationship with her favourite pillow is interrupted by her mother. She then embarks on a strange journey through Mumbai, where her friendships, desires and sense of reality begin to shift.

The abandoned pillow also takes on a life of its own, adding a surreal element to the story as the protagonist searches for love and connection in an increasingly unfamiliar city. Aastha Tiku on the idea behind Dreamboat Tiku, who previously worked as the writer of the 2021 film Sherni, said the story originated from a dream and gradually developed into a screenplay.

“Dreamboat literally came to me in a dream and I spent a few months trying to decipher it and mould it into a screenplay. I wanted the world of the film to feel relatable, at the same time coded in dream logic,” she said.

Explaining the central relationship in the film, Tiku added, “Through the fantasy genre with a female protagonist the intent was to capture the relationship of an artist and her muse - a pillow. The film allowed me to follow my instincts and make something honest, punk and experiential.” Amit Masurkar backs Tiku’s directorial debut The film is produced by Tiku and National Award-winning filmmaker Amit Masurkar, whose credits include Newton, Sherni and Sulemani Keeda.

Masurkar said the film’s unusual premise and visual approach attracted him to the project.

“What drew me to Dreamboat was its unconventional premise and the treatment boards Aastha had prepared for the film. I love how she used pop culture, music, colour, language, fashion to create this campy and surreal fever dream,” he said.

“We are excited to begin our festival journey with DIFF,” he added. Sofia Ashraf leads the cast The film features Sofia Ashraf in her lead acting debut. The rapper, artist and activist is known for her protest song Kodaikanal Won’t. She is joined by comedian and digital creator Supriya Joshi, actor Tenzin Dalha and Prayrak Mehta.

Moses Koul and Gurpal Singh are also part of the cast.

Following Dreamboat, Tiku is developing her first feature film as a director, which is scheduled to go on floors in 2027.

The world premiere at DIFF will mark the beginning of Dreamboat’s festival run.

title: Ramayana: Part One to get JioHotstar pay-per-view release following theatrical window
raw_summary:
Ramayana: Part One, produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios, has partnered with JioHotstar to offer audiences in India a separate on-demand viewing option following the film’s theatrical run. The partnership will use a pay-per-view model, allowing viewers to purchase access to the film on JioHotstar after its exclusive theatrical window.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Part One is scheduled to release worldwide in theatres on November 5, including in IMAX 3D. The film will be released in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and English.

Following its theatrical run, audiences in India will be able to purchase the film separately on JioHotstar through its dedicated on-demand offering. The platform said the film will be available across supported devices and in the highest quality supported by the service. Nita Ambani on bringing Ramayana to audiences Nita M. Ambani, Chairperson, JioStar, said the partnership would help take the cinematic adaptation of the epic to audiences beyond theatres.

“Ramayana is one of India’s greatest civilisational treasures - a story that has shaped our conscience, inspired our imagination, and guided the way we live for centuries. As India enters a new era of storytelling, we have an extraordinary opportunity to carry our cultural legacy forward,” she said.

She added, “At JioHotstar, our vision is to use technology to bring the finest stories within reach of every Indian. It is our privilege to present this grand cinematic vision of Ramayana to families across the country, and introduce a new generation to its eternal values of duty, love, courage, and goodness.” Namit Malhotra on the digital partnership Namit Malhotra, producer, filmmaker and founder and CEO of DNEG, said the film was designed to be experienced on a large screen, particularly in IMAX 3D. However, he noted that cinema infrastructure does not provide access to every audience member.

“I believe Ramayana should be experienced on the biggest screen possible, in IMAX 3D. But our country’s cinema infrastructure cannot reach everyone who holds this epic close. Ramayana belongs to every Indian, and our ambition must reflect that,” Malhotra said.

Explaining the decision to partner with JioHotstar, he added, “JioHotstar has time and again shown how technology can bring a nation together through its sports and entertainment offering. That made them a natural partner to take Ramayana into people’s hands and living rooms, after its theatrical run.” About Ramayana: Part One Ramayana is planned as a two-part live-action cinematic adaptation directed by Nitesh Tiwari. Shridhar Raghavan adapted the screenplay from Valmiki’s epic.

Prime Focus Studios is producing the film in association with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations. The project brings together composers Hans Zimmer and A. R. Rahman, while Ravi Bansal and Ramsey Avery have worked on production design. Terry Notary and Guy Norris choreographed the action.

The cast features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor and Kajal Aggarwal are also part of the ensemble.

Ramayana: Part One will release worldwide in cinemas on November 5, 2026, during the Diwali period. Details regarding the film’s JioHotstar pay-per-view price and availability date after the theatrical window have not been announced yet.

title: No football, no gym, no restaurants? Tiger Shroff shooting raises a FRIGHTENING question: Are Bollywood stars becoming PRISONERS of their own fame?
raw_summary:
For Tiger Shroff, playing football has always been more than just a recreational activity. The actor, known for his extraordinary fitness and athletic abilities, has frequently been spotted enjoying the sport with friends.

On Sunday, October 18, he was doing precisely that. It was supposed to be another ordinary evening. Tiger had finished playing football at a ground in Juhu and was preparing to leave when unidentified assailants opened fire near his vehicle. Tiger escaped unhurt, but his driver and a bystander were injured.

The incident has understandably raised questions about Bollywood’s security arrangements, the threats faced by prominent actors and the possible involvement of organised crime. But there is another question that deserves serious consideration.

What happens when even the simplest activities in a Bollywood star’s life become potential security risks? And, perhaps more importantly, what does this mean for the culture of celebrity photography that has become an inseparable part of Bollywood?

Imagine being unable to step outside your home without planning your movements, checking security arrangements or wondering whether somebody is watching. For most people, playing football, visiting a gym, meeting friends at a café or going out for dinner are ordinary activities. For celebrities, however, even these moments have increasingly become public events.

The irony in Tiger’s case is particularly striking. Here is an actor whose entire professional identity revolves around strength, agility, martial arts and performing extraordinary action sequences. On screen, he regularly overcomes seemingly impossible situations. Yet the real-life incident occurred after something as simple as a football game.

The contrast is unsettling. No amount of physical fitness or martial arts training can eliminate the dangers posed by armed violence. And if an actor begins to feel that an ordinary football outing requires extensive security arrangements, the implications extend far beyond one individual.

What happens to the freedom to live spontaneously? Will actors eventually have to give up activities they have enjoyed for years? Will they have to restrict their movements to private facilities? Will something as simple as meeting friends require advance security coordination?

There was a time when seeing a film star outside a cinema screen was a relatively rare experience. Today, celebrity sightings have become an entertainment industry of their own. From airport arrivals and gym entrances to restaurant exits and family outings, virtually every movement of a major star is social-media content.

Consider a typical paparazzi video. It may reveal where an actor exercises, which restaurant they frequently visit, when they leave home or the route they routinely take. Individually, these details may appear harmless. But when repeated over weeks or months, publicly available information can reveal patterns. In Tiger’s case, investigators have reportedly examined whether the attackers had studied his movements and were familiar with his football routine.

There is no established evidence that paparazzi photographs or videos helped the attackers. It would be unfair and irresponsible to suggest otherwise. Nevertheless, the incident raises a legitimate question: Should Bollywood reconsider how casually the precise locations and daily routines of celebrities are shared?

After an incident as serious as the Tiger Shroff shooting, perhaps this relationship needs to evolve. The solution cannot be to blame photographers for criminal acts they did not commit. Nor should it involve unreasonable restrictions on legitimate journalism. However, it may be time for the industry to distinguish between photographing a public appearance and making someone’s private movements unnecessarily predictable.

There is another possible consequence. If security concerns intensify, celebrities could become increasingly inaccessible. Actors may begin using private entrances, travelling in secured vehicles, avoiding public recreational facilities and limiting informal interactions with fans. Even occasions that currently feel spontaneous could become carefully managed appearances.

In one sense, heightened security may be necessary for individuals facing credible threats. But it could also change Bollywood’s culture.

The most important aspect of this debate is perhaps the least visible. Security isn’t merely about employing guards or installing surveillance cameras. Living under a credible threat can affect an individual’s everyday choices and sense of independence. Ordinary pleasures may require careful planning. Family outings could become complicated. Even familiar environments might begin to feel less comfortable.

Psychologists who work with people exposed to violence often discuss how traumatic incidents can lead to heightened vigilance, anxiety and changes in behaviour. This does not mean Tiger Shroff is experiencing any of these reactions. His personal response is private, and it would be inappropriate to speculate.

But it highlights the broader human cost that can accompany serious security threats. Celebrities may enjoy extraordinary privilege, wealth and public admiration. Yet those advantages cannot fully compensate for the loss of personal freedom.

And that raises a deeply uncomfortable question about the future of celebrity life. If even an ordinary football game becomes a security concern, what happens to the freedom that the rest of us take for granted?

Bollywood’s stars may belong to millions of fans on the big screen. But surely, beyond the cameras, they deserve the freedom to live their own lives.

It will also revisit his 1953 campaign against the permit system in Jammu and Kashmir and the circumstances surrounding his death in detention.

Combining elements of historical drama and political thriller, Syama – The Missing Chapter seeks to examine the decisions and convictions that shaped Dr. Mukherjee's public life. The project also aims to revisit a chapter of India's political history and introduce his ideas and legacy to a new generation of viewers.

Speaking about the project, producer Aditya Kumar Halwasiya said, “Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee’s life is a powerful reminder that true leadership lies in courage, conviction and service to the nation.
